25:- Siding/exteriors/decks (batch 5, 9 candidates, 2026-09-09): new segment. Owner-led exterior shops where estimators double as crew leads; free-estimate funnels and storm-surge inquiries compete with long on-site installs, so follow-up is the leak. Two published emails found (DeckTec, GS Exterior Experts email redacted as placeholder); rest are form/phone-first.
26:- Junk removal/hauling (batch 5, 10 candidates, 2026-09-09): new segment. Same-day/next-day booking is the whole product and runs on phone and text; most are tiny owner-led crews (one is literally one person), so missed calls during jobs are instant lost revenue. Three site-published emails (Super Junkers, Gone For Good, Pride N Service); rest are booking-widget or phone-first. Note: Buffalo's Construction & Landscaping (Facebook pipeline) lists junk haul-off, keep them under Facebook rather than duplicating here.
28:- Water damage restoration (batch 4, 10 candidates, 2026-09-08): new segment. Double seasonal peak, spring snowmelt/summer storms plus winter pipe bursts; nearly every shop sells 24/7 emergency response with 60-minute arrival claims, so flood-crisis callers work down a Google list until someone answers. Extremely phone-first segment, few published emails, forms plus phone are the main routes. Fragmented independents (Abbotts, RestoreCo, Restoration Logistics, AquaRescue) handle insurance claims directly, so paperwork drag is a real pitch angle. 4 of 10 are phone-only with unverified numbers from directory listings; treat those as softer candidates.
34:- Irrigation & sprinkler (batch 1, 11 candidates, 2026-09-09): new segment. Mid-September is the ramp-up to Denver's winterization season (average first hard freeze around October 8, blowout window roughly late September through mid-November); multiple shops warn October appointments fill fast. Pricing observed on company sites runs $85 flat (Mile Hi Services, multi-trade, excluded) to $150 per blowout (Sprinkler Doctor), a high-margin, high-volume, short-window service. Shops skew heavily owner-operator or small family crews (Conrad Olivier at 5280 Sprinklers, Hawkins Brothers, Dave Ferdon's Thornton Sprinklers) who answer their own phones while in the field, the perfect missed-call pain profile: a homeowner who gets voicemail during a freeze warning books the next name on the list, and the shop loses both the blowout and the spring startup. Several shops already push text-first or online booking (303 Sprinklers, 5280 Sprinklers, Sprinkler Doctor), signaling they feel inbound strain. Skip patterns logged: national franchises (Conserva Irrigation), multi-trade companies where blowouts are a side offering (Mile Hi Services, Omni Landscape, Denver Lawn & Snow Care), fire-suppression sprinkler companies (Denver Fire Pro), and directory-only operations with no real site (Gorman's Sprinklers Too, KHEN Sprinklers). Verification caveats kept: Thornton "Sprinklers" (Dave Ferdon) dropped entirely, no own site found; Preferred Sprinklers recorded as form-route only since its directory phone never appeared on its own site.
35:- Kitchen & bath / countertops (batch 1, 13 candidates, 2026-09-09): new segment, kept distinct from the earlier general-remodeler batch. Segment is consult-driven high-ticket sales: free in-home estimates, design consultations, showroom appointments, laser measurements. Most shops are small family crews who live on the tools and cannot answer mid-install. Mid-September is a fall planning window: homeowners want work scheduled before the holidays, contractors want pipelines filled before winter. BathHound was actively advertising 50% off installation and locked 2026 pricing, pointing to live lead capture and price-sensitive comparison shopping. Contact routes skew phone-plus-email; one owner explicitly published (Sarah Ocasek at Blackbird Kitchen and Bath). Excluded per segment rules: Re-Bath Denver (franchise), Northbuilt Construction (general remodeler), Thurston Kitchen + Bath (cabinet/appliance showroom with no install-crew evidence), Coronado Bath and Tile (unreliable contact info). Near-misses needing one more own-site check if the pipeline needs topping up: Kitchen Masters (Lakewood), C & C Kitchens (Denver), 5280 Stone Company (Frederick).
38:- Foundation/masonry/drywall (batch 7, 25 candidates, 2026-09-09): new segments. Foundation repair & basement/crawlspace waterproofing (6 candidates): Mid-September 2026 is prime inspection season in Denver metro: monsoon rains and summer watering have swollen the area's expansive clay soils, so homeowners are discovering seepage, wall cracks, bowing basement walls, and drainage failures right as the pre-freeze window opens. Foundation and waterproofing jobs are high-ticket and almost always won or lost at first contact, and the owner-led shops here are typically in the field on jobs all day. Segment is clean of national brands in the small-shop tier (Groundworks, Thrasher, Ram Jack dealers all skipped as corporate/franchise). Watch for lead-broker style sites ("our network's experts" copy) that look like contractors but are not. Masonry & stucco (10 candidates): Mid-September 2026 is the last good stretch of Denver's exterior work window, and freeze-thaw season is approaching fast, exactly when homeowners discover cracked stucco, failing tuckpointing, and leaky chimney crowns, driving a rush of repair inquiries. Most shops are family-run crews of one to five people with the owner on the scaffold or at the job site, so incoming calls routinely go to voicemail or get answered after hours. Core pitch fit: AI call capture answers every ring, qualifies the repair, and books the free estimate, while automated follow-up keeps quotes from going cold. Skip pattern: multi-state branded stucco sites and larger remodelers that bundle stucco as one of many trades. Drywall & texture (9 candidates): September is the pivot point in Colorado as exterior work winds down and homeowners turn to basements, texture re-dos, popcorn ceiling removal, and water-damage repairs, so these shops want to keep crews busy with interior projects. The market is fragmented: dozens of owner-led shops of one to twenty people, most taking intake by phone or a basic contact form, many owners doubling as estimator and scheduler. Strongest fits are owner-operators (Benjamin at B&D Drywall, owner-run Flow Drywall) where every missed call is missed revenue; already-staffed firms are lower priority. Stay excluded: franchise systems (PatchMaster, Hole in the Wall, All Four Walls) whose local operators have less buying authority, plus thin AI-template sites and no-own-site directory-only operations.
44:- Plumbing (Western Colorado, batch 13, 2026-09-09): new segment, 2 verified candidates. Shops are overwhelmingly phone-first; smaller independents rarely publish an email or form on their own sites, so the strict own-site rule throttled yield. Mid-September 2026 is shoulder season: irrigation/swamp-cooler work winding down, boiler and heating service about to ramp, second-home and short-term-rental turnover steady in resort markets. Regional players in Montrose and Grand Junction skew family-owned multi-tech with 15-30 years of history; Cortez, Gunnison, Craig, Meeker run thinner with owner-operators.
45:- HVAC (Western Colorado, batch 13, 2026-09-09): new segment, 10 verified candidates. Independent, family-run, and employee-owned shops rather than national chains, anchored in Grand Junction, Montrose, Glenwood Springs with spokes into Aspen, Basalt, Durango, Hotchkiss, Cortez. September is the hinge month: furnace tune-ups, install-quote follow-up, first-cold-snap breakdowns, plus ski-town second homes needing reliable service from absentee owners. Nearly every shop runs its own site with a working contact form or published email, so direct outreach is practical. Skip patterns: phone-only own sites, parked/dead/hijacked domains, directory-only listings, and a Wheat Ridge-headquartered branch (Major Heating) deprioritized as not clearly local.
52:- Snow removal (Western Colorado, batch 15, 2026-09-10): new segment, 5 verified candidates. Mid-September lands squarely in the snow contract-signing window (September through November), the segment's highest-intent inbound period. Own-site evidence documents storm cleanups starting 2-3am with 14-16 hour storm days; storm-morning call chaos, route-capacity pressure, early-hour dispatch, and seasonal contract renewals are the missed-call pain PING targets. Commercial operators with multi-crew routes (D&D Asphalt, Summit Sweeping, Grasshoppers) are the strongest fits. Thinner than expected under the own-site rule; mostly landscaping/asphalt hybrids, phone-primary. If the pool thins, revisit phone-primary near-misses (Peaceful Valley, J&J Snow Removal) or Facebook engagement.
53:- Roofing (Western Colorado, batch 15, 2026-09-10): new segment, 11 verified candidates. Late-summer hail season winding down but roofers are in their busiest insurance-claim and free-inspection quarter; crews on roofs all day while phones go unanswered, so first-to-answer wins the claim. Coverage concentrated in Montrose (6), Grand Junction (2), Glenwood Springs (2), Durango (1), Gunnison (1); smaller markets yielded only directory/phone-only listings. Pattern: thin WordPress/Squarespace sites where the contact form is the only digital front door; several openly post Gmail/Yahoo addresses, signaling they live in their inboxes. Watch for lookalike regional chains and templated city pages.
54:- Electrical (Western Colorado, batch 17, 2026-09-10): new segment, 6 verified candidates. September is the pre-heating and pre-winter reliability window: generator evaluations, panel upgrades, service calls, second-home winterization, lighting and shade automation projects, and 24/7 emergency positioning all peak at once. Resort and mountain shops (Steamboat, Glenwood Springs, Durango, Bayfield) sell high-end residential and automation work where qualification and routing matter more than raw lead volume. Owner-led field work with phone/form intake is the norm; pitch reliable capture while electricians are on jobs, not replacing technical judgment. Skip patterns: lead-broker style "electrical network" sites (Duft/Colorado Electrical Network), generic SEO-location pages, and larger multi-tech firms that dilute the owner-led fit (R&A Enterprises included with a size caveat).
56:- Duct / dryer vent + commercial janitorial (Western CO, batch 22, 2026-09-10): new segments, 5 verified (3 duct: Advanced Duct Cleaning Durango, Mr. Vac Glenwood/GJ, Rapid Response GJ; 1 janitorial: JP Cleaning Services Glenwood; 1 multi-trade: Timberline Enterprises Gunnison). Duct runs WordPress across all qualifiers, no CRM signals; segment is nearly complete with 2 strong near-misses left (GJ Dryer Vent Cleaning, Quick Draw Cleaning) worth one verification pass on booking/form fields. Janitorial is thin: Elite Cleaning Service (GJ, 70+ employees, commercial-only) is the highest-value next verification target, then Green Space Cleaning and Commercial Cleaners. Segment heat: pre-heating-season is the duct rush window (furnace cleanings, dryer-vent fire-safety calls before winter); janitorial bids and recurring commercial cleanings live or die on response speed.
58:- Septic / well / pump (Western Colorado, research batch round 23, 2026-09-11): new segment, 9 qualified. Septic pumping runs on 2 to 5 year recall cycles plus emergency demand; several shops promise free estimates and same-day/emergency service, creating the missed-call pain. 24/7 emergency positioning is everywhere but several shops run office-only hours; after-hours calls are the clearest AI receptionist angle. Durango is a septic hot spot (Durango Septic, Mountain Septic, LePew Four Corners, Alpenglow Gunnison). Well and pump shops (San Juan Pump, Valley Pump) have water-outage urgency: a homeowner with no water calls the next shop if the first rings out. Durango Septic literally brands on answering the phone ("the last thing you want is a voicemail") with a small crew in the field. No scheduling software observed anywhere in the segment; software grades UNKNOWN across the board. Segment is nearly all phone-only (8 of 9); only San Juan Pump (Montrose) has an unblocked contact form, though it is a customer form with no B2B invitation.
59:- Excavation / dirtwork / grading (Western Colorado, research batch round 23, 2026-09-11): new segment, 11 qualified. Demand clusters: site preparation, foundations, grading and drainage, septic installation, utility trenching, demolition, hauling, land clearing. Pitch angles: missed bid requests, estimate follow-up, permit coordination, site-evaluation scheduling, routing residential versus commercial inquiries. Five phone-only operators are most exposed while crews run equipment. Tate Civil (Glenwood) stakes a stated one-business-day inquiry response, a strong speed-to-lead angle. Metcalf (Parachute) runs seasonal intake (spring/summer reclamation and stormwater, fall/winter road and emergency ops). Software: Wix x2, WordPress, GoDaddy x2 CONFIRMED (site platform only); no booking widgets or CRM badges anywhere; rest UNKNOWN. Earthworx (Montrose) has an unblocked customer contact form; Aspen Digger and Miles Rippy have real contact pages.
62:- Asphalt / paving (Western Colorado, research batch round 24, 2026-09-11): new segment, 8 qualified. September is the tail of Colorado's paving season (May through October); sealcoat needs sustained pavement temps above 50F, so HOA and commercial lot rush before winter is the urgent demand trigger. Crews are on pavers, rollers, and sealcoat rigs all day and cannot answer; estimate follow-up is the pitch. Grand Junction is crowded; Glenwood/Rifle/Carbondale and Durango/Cortez/Pagosa coverage is thinner; Cortez, Pagosa Springs, Craig, and Meeker produced no own-site-verified shops. Software UNKNOWN across all 17 researched; no booking widgets or CRM badges anywhere. Skip patterns: franchise systems (Jet-Black), white-label template farms (Animas Asphalt's "CPS" copy), out-of-state bases. Several strong local shops have weak or no websites (Kauffman, High Country, JB's, CM Asphalt), which is both a pipeline gap and an inbound angle: thin web presence correlates with phone-only workflows and high missed-call pain.
63:- Garage doors (Denver metro, research batch round 24, 2026-09-11): new segment (outward expansion), 9 qualified. Broken torsion springs are the single most urgent trigger; a door stuck open is a security emergency. Several shops advertise 24/7 but run daytime-only offices, so after-hours missed-call capture is the clean pitch. Segment is saturated with templated city-page SEO farms and a national franchise layer (A1, Precision, Dave's); Colorado-ownership verification stays mandatory. Watch address-sharing brands (A1 Garage Door Service shares 5081 Kingston St with Don's Garage Door Repair). Shops show little evidence of Housecall Pro style booking wizards; most routes are plain phone numbers or simple WordPress forms, so lead with missed-call capture rather than booking-friction relief. 7 Denver-area near-misses (Arvada Garage Door, AVI, Incredible, Mile High Sales & Repair, Garage Door Knights, DMAC, Gold Label Door) are BBB-listed with no own website; qualify on own-site discovery.
64:- Solar installers (Western Colorado, research batch round 25, 2026-09-11): new segment, 9 qualified. Richest new Western Slope segment this round. Federal tax credits expired 12/31/2025 (stated on Solar Design Group's own site), so every remaining lead costs more to win, which is the core capture/follow-up argument. Shops are small, consultative, permit-heavy: utility usage analysis, permits, interconnection, net metering, PTO, monitoring-app handoff (Atlasta); rebate paperwork for GEO and LPEA (Durango Solar Works); 4CORE Home Upgrade program network creates rebate-paperwork load in the southwest. Orphaned-system repair is a real sub-market (Sunsense markets rescue of systems installed by other firms; Shaw and High Noon sell maintenance contracts). Software UNKNOWN across all; no Aurora/OpenSolar/Sighten/Snugg Pro, no CRM or booking widgets anywhere. Skip patterns: regional multi-state operators (Big Dog Solar), parked domains (Four Corners Solar), national location pages, placeholder-data sites (SoL Energy).
65:- Insulation (Western Colorado, research batch round 25, 2026-09-11): new segment, 1 qualified (Eagle Insulation, Durango, robert@eagleinsulationco.com). Pool is genuinely thin under the own-site rule: 11 near-misses logged, most established GJ firms are phone-only own sites or directory-only. Durango/Pagosa spray foam scene is tied to mountain-town winterization and second-home work; 4CORE preferred-contractor list is the pressure point (rebate and energy-efficiency questions create qualification load). Seasonal timing favorable (mid-September pre-heating-season weatherization rush). Pitch: field-heavy crews publish same-day or 24-hour callback promises; instant-response lead capture is the concrete angle. Expect future insulation batches to stay small.
67:- Siding / exteriors / decks & outdoor living (Western Colorado, round 42, 2026-09-13): brand-new WCO segment. The pipeline covered WCO roofing, concrete, and fencing but never siding or deck specialists. Discovery leaned on GJ vinyl siding shops and Durango deck builders; Montrose siding work runs through roofing/siding combos with no published own site. Near-misses are concentrated here and one browser fetch failed, so the next pass should be a live on-site contact-route verification before any outreach. Grand Valley Seamless Siding and CL Deck and Porches are the two cleanest segment fits.
68:- House cleaning / maid services (Western Colorado, round 42, 2026-09-13): brand-new WCO segment; prior house-cleaning work was Denver-metro only, and WCO cleaning coverage stopped at carpet, duct, and commercial janitorial. The segment is rich in small owner-led shops with phone-only listings, which matches the missed-call angle precisely. Elite Cleaning Service (70+ employees, weekly recurring base) is the highest-value target; La Plata Cleaning carries a live missed-inquiry review signal. Franchises (Merry Maids GJ) and broker platforms (Walmart house cleaning, Care.com, Thumbtack, Turno, Homeaglow) were excluded. Sparkling and Beyond RE-VERIFIED from the 2026-09-13 archive (own-site email + phone now confirmed on its FAQ page) but held on WATCH: its site shows TN and IA city pages, so local ownership must be verified before any outreach.
69:- Epoxy / concrete coatings (Western Colorado, round 55, 2026-09-14): brand-new WCO segment. Independent pool is genuinely thin once chains are removed: national/regional systems (Garage Kings, GarageFloorCoating.com dealer network with pages for nearly every Western Slope town, Spartan Floor Coatings) dominate search visibility. Remaining independents are small owner-operated shops in the northwest and mountain corridors (Craig, Steamboat, Roaring Fork, Pagosa), plus painters for whom epoxy floor coatings are a secondary line (Mountain Sky Closets and Garages, Todd Hill Painting, Sloop Painting). Recurring pattern: phone-only intake, no email/form/follow-up machinery, which is exactly the missed-call opening but only WATCH-grade until verified per business. Pre-winter pitch angle supported by multiple coating sites (garage floor protection against snowmelt, road salts, freeze-thaw), but keep it generic, not personalized, until a business-specific problem is verified. Skip patterns: chain/dealer systems (Garage Kings, GarageFloorCoating.com pages, Spartan), out-of-state SEO location pages (Florida company running a Cortez page), generic lead-gen toll-free pages, athletic-court-only resurfacing, Front Range companies.
70:- Awning / shade / patio covers (Western Colorado, round 55, 2026-09-14): brand-new WCO segment. Specialist pool is genuinely sparse as of September 2026: two deep specialists verified (Canvas Shade in GJ, third-generation since 1949, structured multi-step intake form, owner named on site, the clearest WARM in the pool; Durango Shade Company, Wix site, motorized shade systems by phone), two Montrose-area owner-operators (Alpine Shades, motorized/smart-home products, phone-only; Colorado Awning and Screen, Eclipse retractable specialist, own site failed to render this round), one GJ retractable-awning specialist (Western Slope Shading Solutions, WordPress, no own-site contact found), one Glenwood contractor (Daybreak, aging site, awning is one service line, revamp candidate). Mid-September timing is tail-end for shade sales season (commercial restaurant patio enclosures and residential shade sails sell hardest in spring/early summer); fall angle is commercial patio enclosure and off-season planning. Skip patterns: interior window-treatment showrooms (Ambassador Blind, Shades Done Right, Budget Blinds, Gotcha Covered = franchises), general deck/fence builders, Front Range companies, national manufacturers, directory/lead-broker pages, tent manufacturers.
71:- Pest control (Western Colorado, research batch round 68, 2026-09-16): new geography for an old segment. Vertebrate specialists (prairie-dog crews) and one family pest shop in GJ; most are directory-only or phone-only, so the strict own-site rule kept the pest batch small (4). Pool/spa/hot tub (Western Colorado, research batch round 68, 2026-09-16): 11 qualified, the richest WCO batch in several rounds. Three CONFIRMED stack finds: HubSpot forms on Colorado Pool + Spa Scapes (response-speed gap, not lead-volume), Wix on Four Corners Stoves and Spa, MyPoolPortal customer portal on Telluride Spa Care (portal angle dead, AI answering and route scheduling open). Route-based trades with strong missed-call angles; several owner-led shops with no websites at all (Tub Tech Spas, operating since 1987). Eight directory-only records have blank contact fields per the no-guessing rule.
73:- Mobile/field welding (Western Colorado, round 74, 2026-09-17): brand-new WCO segment. GJ anchor shops (Clemmer, All Metals, Pfeiffer, JCW, Duke's) plus a thin Rifle-area directory pool; two own-site email routes found (Clemmer's info@clemmerwelding.com and All Metals' ryan@allmetalswelding.com), the rest phone-only or directory-thin. Segment heat: moderate and steady, tied to oilfield, ag, and construction maintenance rather than consumer demand; September lands in the pre-winter maintenance window when equipment and pipe repairs spike. Pitch angle: 24/7 field shops lose emergency repair calls while the crew is on a job, so always-on call capture has the most defensible ROI; larger industrial shops (Clemmer) are less owner-operated and need a consultative read before outreach. Skip pattern: Denver/front-range mobile welders (Pegasus, O C Welding) and delinquent entities (G2G Mobile Welding) are out of region or dead; Breck Ironworks is a geographic near-miss.
74:- Smart-home / security-system installers (Western Colorado, round 74, 2026-09-17): brand-new WCO segment. Independent pool is thin and fragmented: GJ has Superior Alarm Inc, Fire Team Security, EyeCamTech and a handful of small AV/surveillance shops; Durango shows directory-thin AV/security names; Montrose/Telluride show Superior Alarm & Fire Protection, a distinct entity from GJ's Superior Alarm Inc. Segment heat: moderate; alarm shops run phone-only intake competing against Vivint and ADT on local trust, and a 3-star or lower review mentioning phone or response issues is a strong trigger for this trade. Pitch angle: after-hours alarm and camera calls go to voicemail while techs are on installs, so missed-call capture plus fast callback is the core ROI story; website revamp is secondary (several sites are thin or template-built). Skip pattern: multi-state ADT dealer models with local offices stay WATCH only; MSPs masquerading as security shops (CommWest) and directory-only listings with no own site stay at WATCH. Note: Superior Alarm Inc and Commwest were already pipeline NEW from round 52; this round re-verified own-site phone (970-245-0962) and own-site email/phone (concierge@commwestcorp.com, 970-242-8124) instead of creating duplicate rows.
75:- General contractors / remodelers (Western Colorado, round 84, 2026-09-18): brand-new WCO segment (prior remodeling rows were Denver-metro only). Yield concentrated where the geography was weighted: Roaring Fork Valley (McSwain Builders Aspen, Franklin Remodeling Carbondale, Down Valley Design Center Rifle) plus the southwest corner (Elevation Custom Builders Durango, Altitude Renovation Durango, Top Drawer Construction Durango). Segment heat: mid-September is the pre-winter planning window, homeowners want projects scoped and booked before the holidays, GCs want pipelines filled before freeze; consult-style intake with design consultations, estimate requests, and project-inquiry forms is the norm, so intake-detail capture, scheduling, client updates, and after-hours missed-call capture are the pitch angles. Only 7 qualified because the strict live-verification rule held: many real shops (DM Neuman, Aspen Built, Durango Remodeling, Kaegebein, Divide Creek, Stewart, Asher, Ponderosa) publish no email and expose no form in fetchable text, and several own-site fetches failed outright. One KNOWN stack find: Buildertrend at McSwain (project platform, automation gap around intake/scheduling/client updates, not around the platform itself). Skip patterns: Hurst Construction (Cortez) domain now serves a generic lead-broker template, treat its web presence as compromised; large firms, civil-first contractors, franchises, nonprofits.
81:- Fence-staining restoration + log-home restoration (round 127, 2026-09-23): two new segments, honest yield 2 of 15-25 target. Pencil Log Pros (GJ, office@pencillogpros.com own-site email, owner Brad Siler, 16+ employees, CONFIRMED confidence) is the log-home specialist anchor; Every Fence GJ (fencerepairgj.com own-site form, Weebly STRONG INDICATION, WATCH) is the fence-staining fit. Late September is the final reliable exterior staining window before cold/wet weather; log-home work is in the fall pre-winter inspection/sealing window. Surfaces are thin: fence-staining dominated by broad painters, lead-broker directories (OutdoorNearMe, Porch), out-of-area firms (R&J Painting = Illinois; FenceMakeover = Front Range; Pure Pressure = Northern CO round-89 exclusion), already-tracked names (RJ's Painting, Valleywide, Just Fencing, Taylor Fence, Top Choice), no-own-site specialists (StainMisters GJ, Mountain Life Custom Staining Montrose), one hijacked-content site (Final Touch Painting renders VA roofing copy). Log-home near-misses: kit manufacturer/builder Frontier Log Homes (Montrose, off-segment), identity-conflicted Mountain State Log Homes, out-of-geography specialists (Jorgensen SD, Tuks Steamboat). New-business radar: The Screen Medic (screen repair/install) opened a new GJ location (1700 I-70BL #2), ribbon-cut by GJ Area Chamber 2026-09-23, expansion of existing Montrose shop (NOT a new filing); MN name-twin unresolved, recheck chain at outreach time. GJ Chamber ribbon-cutting pipeline is the highest-signal radar channel right now (2 cuttings in 12 days); SOS still JS-only; chamber new-member lists still not surfaced. FB scan #126 (52 in-window): 1 new prospect (The Yellow handyman services, Delta-area, FB Page route only, message-button check pending); corridor FB trade-promo volume near zero seven windows running. Review intel: 0 triggers across 10-prospect HOT/WARM sample (RAM price-transparency complaint undated = angle material only). AEO: Alpine Pressure STRONG (already AEO-literate, not an opportunity); RAM MODERATE (review-volume + town/service FAQ gap); Grime Fighters MODERATE (severe AEO namesake crowding: PA/TN/NC/GA firms dilute identity); Mr Patch MODERATE (strong content trapped on Google Sites/Wix subdomains, own-domain migration opportunity).
706:- Fox Hot Tubs Billiards & Games | hot tub retail and supplies | Edwards | foxhottubs@gmail.com (published repeatedly on own-site product pages) | unknown | storefront business; own-site size details limited | Retail-first shop with a Gmail contact is reachable but lower on service-pain signals; keep as retail-segment filler unless the own site adds repair evidence. | QUEUED 2026-09-10 (round-15 email draft; behind email FIFO queue)
802:- Painting contractors (Western Colorado, batch 19, 2026-09-10): new segment, 7 verified candidates. Mid-September is the last exterior window before cold plus interior-repaint ramp-up; early-fall splits crews between interior and exterior work, so missed estimate requests during on-ladder hours and slow consult-form follow-up are the pitch. Most qualified shops publish Gmail addresses on their own sites, so email-first outreach is natural. Coverage: Grand Junction/Mesa County (SunShine, Top Choice, WBS industrial, St. Bella in Montrose), Durango (Prime, San Juan Custom, NHBRHOOD). No verifiable qualifiers in Gunnison, Glenwood Springs, Rifle, Carbondale, Aspen, Steamboat Springs, Craig, or Meeker despite active searching. Skip patterns: phone-only own sites, directory-only operators (Mortensen Painting, Silt, 23 years, no own site), chains/stores, national lead pages.
803:- Tree care / arborists (Western Colorado, batch 19, 2026-09-10): new segment, 6 verified candidates. Entering the fall hazard-tree and pre-winter pruning window, with storm-damage and fire-mitigation work still warm in Durango and the Grand Valley; 24/7 emergency positioning (Top Notch, Tree Climbers) makes after-hours missed-call capture the sharpest angle. Pool is partial-form heavy: 4 of 6 routes need one more field read before drafting (verify address/CAPTCHA/service-selects). Notable: Alpine Tree Service and T4 Tree Services both folded into SavATree and were excluded as acquisitions; Lorax Tree Service (Durango) excluded for a form requiring street address plus reCAPTCHA. 7 near-misses with live own sites (Mission Ready Trees, McKay Tree Service, Quala-Tree Care, Binkley & Sons Painting, Integrity Painting, Sonrise Painting & Remodeling, Forest Scapes LLC) queued for a contact-page verification pass in research-scratch-round19.md.
804:- Concrete contractors / flatwork (Western Colorado, batch 21, 2026-09-10): new segment, 9 verified candidates across Rifle, Grand Junction (2), Glenwood Springs, Steamboat Springs, Pagosa Springs, Cortez, Carbondale, Durango; none in Fruita, Palisade, Clifton, Delta, Gunnison, Craig, Meeker. Fall is foundation-before-freeze and winter-prep repair season (polyjacking, sealing, slab work); missed estimate requests while crews are on pours is the sharp angle. 5 of 9 publish a direct email, 4 rest on forms. Notable: Advanced Concrete Solutions runs an ACI-certified crew with named team members (easy personalization); Giovonni Construction doubles as a snow-management shop. Skip patterns: phone/fax-only contact pages, ready-mix suppliers with no consumer route, chains, aggregator pages.
805:- Carpet & upholstery cleaning (Western Colorado, batch 21, 2026-09-10): new segment, only 2 verified under the strict own-site rule (Grand Junction, Delta); nearly every Western Colorado carpet shop is phone-only, and several domains are dead or hijacked (DeJulio's to a gambling site, Black Bear to a casino site, Rash & Son parked). ProTeck Carpet (Delta) shows STRONG INDICATION GoHighLevel (leadconnectorhq.com assets) while routing web leads through a generic form, a strong consultative angle for a shop already on GHL.
1089:- Research notes: only 3 of the 8-12 target qualified under the strict own-site rule (email or verified form required). 6 near-misses logged in research-scratch-round32-locksmiths.md for later re-verification (Durango Lock and Key, Pagosa Armor Locksmith, Simmons Lock & Key, Tri-County Locksmith, Gene's Lock and Key, S&S Lock Service).
